title: Check the version of an installed program
summary: Print the version of a program installed on your computer, such as git, so you can compare it with the version a guide asks for. These commands only read information and change nothing.

aliases.text: what version of git do I have
see installed software version in terminal
how to check app version in terminal
как проверить версию программы в терминале

prerequisites: Know the program name as you type it in the terminal, for example git

steps.explain: Check that the program is installed and see where it is. Nothing printed means the program is not installed or not in your PATH.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM
placeholders.description: Program name as you type it in the terminal, without the path.

steps.expect: A path such as /usr/bin/git. If nothing is printed, the program is not installed.

steps.explain: Print the installed version. Look for the version number in the first line of the output.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM
placeholders.description: Same program name you checked in the previous step.

steps.expect: One line with the program name and a version number, for example 'git version 2.43.0'.

alternatives.explain: If --version prints an error, show the first lines of the help text. Many programs print their version or usage there.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM
placeholders.description: Same program name you checked in the previous step.

alternatives.expect: The first lines of the help text, usually starting with a usage line. Look for a version number.

warnings: Compare the version with the guide only for the same program. Two different programs can share a name, so check the path shown by the first command.

source.title: bash manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
